item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Sept. 20)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: UMass Dartmouth football player killed in stabbing, student charged with murder
item.description: A UMass Dartmouth football player was killed in a stabbing in Providence and another student has been charged with murder.

item.title: North Korea launches missiles as it dials up pressure against U.S.
item.description: The launches came just days after Pyongyang reasserted its status as a nuclear-armed state and rejected a U.N. resolution demanding it halt its nuclear activities.

item.title: Nature: Utah's Canyonlands National Park
item.description: We leave you this Sunday morning wandering among the red rocks at Canyonlands National Park in Utah. Videographer: Brad Markel.

item.title: Democrat Andy Beshear on pursuing "The Great American Reset"
item.description: The two-term Kentucky Governor advises his fellow Democrats to speak like "normal people" and not shy away from progressive politics or religious faith. He discusses his book, "Go and Do Likewise," which teaches how to change minds by winning hearts.

item.title: Democrat Andy Beshear on pursuing "The Great American Reset"
item.description: Two-term Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear advises his fellow Democrats to speak like "normal people" and not shy away from progressive politics or religious faith. Beshear shares that recipe for success in a deep-red state with "Sunday Morning" national correspondent Robert Costa, and discusses his book, "Go and Do Likewise: How We Heal a Broken Country," which teaches how Democrats can change minds by winning hearts.

item.title: Book excerpt: "Roll the Calls" by Ari Emanuel
item.description: In his memoir, the Hollywood superagent and mogul writes of coming to blows in the competitive entertainment universe – and, in one instance, being sidelined by the business end of a truck.

item.title: U.S. embassies across Middle East issue security alerts for Americans
item.description: The alerts did not cite a specific threat, but called for Americans to "exercise heightened vigilance."

item.title: Passage: Peter Max and Bob Mackie
item.description: "Sunday Morning" looks back on the life of Peter Max, whose psychedelic pop art became synonymous with the 1960s; and remembers costume designer Bob Mackie, who dressed the likes of Cher, Carol Burnett and Diana Ross.

item.title: Superagent Ari Emanuel: Born to fight
item.description: The Hollywood dealmaker is telling his life story in a raw, raunchy and rollicking new memoir, "Roll the Calls." He talks about growing up a bullied, dyslexic kid in the suburbs of Chicago, and explains why he is never afraid of confrontation.

item.title: Charles Spencer on the royal fallout following Princess Diana's death
item.description: In his first interview about his new book, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister," Charles Spencer talks about his attempt to set down what he calls the definitive story of Princess Diana.

item.title: Superagent Ari Emanuel: Born to fight
item.description: Hollywood dealmaker Ari Emanuel is telling his life story in a raw, raunchy and rollicking new memoir, "Roll the Calls." He talks with Turner Classic Movies host Ben Mankiewicz about his rise from the agency mail room to becoming executive chairman of WME Group and executive chair and CEO of TKO. He also talks about growing up a bullied, dyslexic kid in the suburbs of Chicago; becoming the inspiration for Ari Gold in the HBO series "Entourage"; and explains why he is never afraid of confrontation.

item.title: Extended interview: Charles Spencer on Princess Diana
item.description: In his first interview about his new book, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister," Charles Spencer, the 9th Earl Spencer, sits down at his ancestral estate Althorp with correspondent Mark Phillips to talk about Princess Diana, and why he sought to write the definitive story of her life. He also discusses the royals' relationship to Diana, and then-Prince Charles' reaction to her death in 1997.

item.title: Charles Spencer's striking claims about the royal fallout following Princess Diana's death
item.description: In his first interview about his new book, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister," Charles Spencer talks with correspondent Mark Phillips about his attempt to set down what he calls the true history of the life of his sister, Princess Diana. He also talks about Prince Harry's grief after Diana's death, suggesting that a "more understanding treatment" of the young prince at the time might have led to "a happier course ahead."

item.title: A spectacle of puppetry: Buffalo parade through New York City
item.description: This past week, a herd of 40 buffalo roamed the concrete canyons of Lower Manhattan and Brooklyn – life-size puppets that are part of a public arts project by St. Ann's Warehouse, a Brooklyn theater. Correspondent Anthony Mason reports.

item.title: Retiring Smithsonian head Lonnie G. Bunch III: "You can run from history, but you can't hide"
item.description: In 2019, Bunch became both the first historian and the first African American to serve as Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution. As he prepares to retire, he talks about the museums' mission to protect history, and give America a full picture of itself.

item.title: Extended interview: Lonnie G. Bunch III
item.description: In this web exclusive, Secretary of the Smithsonian Lonnie G. Bunch III, who recently announced his retirement, talks with Mo Rocca about the mission of the Smithsonian Institution.

item.title: Retiring Smithsonian head Lonnie Bunch on protecting history
item.description: In 2019, Lonnie G. Bunch III became both the first historian and the first African American to serve as Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution. Now 73, Bunch has announced he is retiring. He talks with correspondent Mo Rocca about fulfilling and enriching the Smithsonian's mandate. He also talks about pressure from the Trump White House questioning the patriotism of Smithsonian staff, and why the museums' mission – to protect history – includes giving America a full picture of itself.

item.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang rejects AI extinction fear as "doomsday narratives"
item.description: Predictions that AI could destroy humanity in a few years are irresponsible and not based on science, Nvidia's co-founder told CBS News.

item.title: Extended interview: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on fears about AI
item.description: In this web exclusive, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang talks with CBS News' Jo Ling Kent about the exponential growth of AI, industry warnings about its power, and why he disagrees with recent calls to slow down development.

item.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang on artificial intelligence
item.description: The Atlantic recently called Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang "the most powerful man in AI." He talks with correspondent Jo Ling Kent at Nvidia headquarters in Santa Clara, Calif., about the latest developments in artificial intelligence and the ongoing debate over safety and regulations.

item.title: 9/20: Sunday Morning
item.description: Hosted by Jane Pauley. Featured: Battling sports gambling addiction; Charles Spencer on his sister, Princess Diana; Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on AI; Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear; Hollywood superagent Ari Emanuel; The Smithsonian's Lonnie Bunch; and a spectacle of buffalo puppetry.

item.title: Trump says proposed arch will also be a "top grade Military Complex"
item.description: President Trump said that he has agreed to convert plans for a massive triumphal arch into a "top grade Military Complex," equipped with snipers and drone storage.

item.title: Sheeran says situation in Gaza is "catastrophic and unjustifiable" at Philly show
item.description: Ed Sheeran opened his solo concert in Philadelphia on Saturday with comments about Gaza, saying what is happening there is "catastrophic and unjustifiable."

item.title: Trump vows to form "AI Force," says he won't allow slowdown of AI development
item.description: In a Truth Social post​, Mr. Trump called fears around artificial intelligence possibly becoming a superintelligence that could pose a threat to human existence a hoax.

item.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico staffers barred from White House after Trump ban
item.description: President Trump said Friday that three outlets would be banned from the White House, "effective immediately."

item.title: 6 takeaways from our interview with the officer shot down in Iran
item.description: In his first interview, Bravo, an Air Force colonel who was shot down in Iran, told 60 Minutes his story of survival and provided new details about the rescue operation.
